title: regional-quant-batch-capacity-scenarios-may2025
body:
Summary and purpose:
This sheet compares candidate deployment scenarios that trade off quantization aggressiveness and batching to hit regional throughput SLAs while bounding quality degradation. It produces GPU counts and cost estimates per region (us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1) for three traffic profiles (interactive-chat, high-throughput-batch, mixed).

Assumptions (shared):
- Target 99th percentile latency SLOs: interactive-chat <= 250ms, mixed <= 450ms, batch <= 1500ms per request (for large batched jobs).
- Baseline model: open-Llama-v2-13B float32 (reference perf).
- Quantization modes: FP32 (baseline), 8-bit int (Q8), 4-bit RTN (Q4), 3-bit dynamic (Q3 -- experimental).
- Batching behavior: continuous batching with max_batch and max_latency knobs. Estimate tokens/sec per GPU varies with batch size and quantization.
- Cost assumptions (monthly): A100-80GB = $9.00/hr, H100-80GB = $13.50/hr, T4 = $1.10/hr. 24/7 month = 730 hrs.
- Safety buffer: +20% headroom for peak and autoscale latency buffer.

Key formulas used (spreadsheet style):
- tokens_per_sec_per_gpu = baseline_tps * quant_speedup * batch_speedup_factor
- effective_throughput_region = tokens_per_sec_per_gpu * GPUs_allocated * (utilization / 100)
- GPUs_needed = ceil( region_required_tps / (tokens_per_sec_per_gpu * (utilization / 100)) ) * 1.2 (apply safety buffer)
- monthly_cost = GPUs_needed * hourly_rate * 730

Baseline reference row (float32, small batch):
- baseline_tps_per_gpu (A100) = 1200 tokens/sec (interactive profile, short context);
- baseline_quality_score = 100 (relative scale)

Scenarios table (per-region consolidated rows):

1) Scenario: Conservative (minimal quant, small batching)
- Quantization: FP32
- Batch config: max_batch 8, max_latency 40ms
- GPU type: A100-80GB
- est tokens/sec/GPU: 1200 (no quant speedup, small batch)
- quality_delta: 0%
- target_utilization: 65%
- us-west1 demand (peak tokens/sec): 5,200
- GPUs_needed (calc): ceil(5200 / (1200 * 0.65)) = ceil(6.67) = 7 -> apply 1.2 buffer => 9 GPUs
- monthly_cost (A100): 9 * 9.0 * 730 = $59,130
- notes: highest quality, highest cost; good baseline for sensitive customers.

2) Scenario: Balanced (Q8 + moderate batching)
- Quantization: Q8 (8-bit)
- Batch config: max_batch 32, max_latency 80ms (sensible for mixed workloads)
- GPU type: A100-80GB (quant helps reduce memory/throughput pressure)
- est tokens/sec/GPU: 1200 * 1.6 (Q8 speedup) * 1.25 (batch) =~ 2400 tps
- quality_delta: -1.8% (relative output-quality score 98.2)
- target_utilization: 75%
- us-west1 demand: 5,200
- GPUs_needed: ceil(5200 / (2400 * 0.75)) = ceil(2.89) = 3 -> buffer => 4 GPUs
- monthly_cost: 4 * 9.0 * 730 = $26,280
- notes: ~55% cost reduction vs conservative; quality impact likely acceptable for most customers; easier autoscale headroom.

3) Scenario: Aggressive quant + large batching (throughput-first)
- Quantization: Q4 (4-bit RTN) with activation-aware calibration
- Batch config: max_batch 128, max_latency 200ms (acceptable for non-interactive jobs)
- GPU type: H100-80GB (better throughput for quantized kernels)
- est tokens/sec/GPU: baseline 1200 * 2.8 (Q4) * 1.8 (batch) =~ 6048 tps (rounded 6000)
- quality_delta: -4.5% (relative quality 95.5)
- target_utilization: 80%
- us-west1 demand: 5,200
- GPUs_needed: ceil(5200 / (6000 * 0.8)) = ceil(1.08) = 2 -> buffer => 3 GPUs
- monthly_cost (H100): 3 * 13.5 * 730 = $29,565
- notes: lowest GPU count; slightly higher cost per GPU but still ~50% cheaper than conservative; requires careful evals for hallucination/regression risk.

4) Scenario: Experimental low-bit (Q3) for cold-batch region (ap-southeast1)
- Quantization: Q3 dynamic (experimental kernel)
- Batch: max_batch 256, max_latency 1200ms (batch processing windows)
- GPU type: H100 or A100 depending on availability (prefer H100 for kernel maturity)
- est tokens/sec/GPU: baseline * 3.6 * 2.0 =~ 8640 tps
- quality_delta: -8% (monitor closely)
- target_utilization: 85%
- example ap-southeast1 demand (batch window): 40,000 tokens/sec sustained for 2 hours peak
- GPUs_needed: ceil(40000 / (8640 * 0.85)) = ceil(5.44) = 6 -> buffer => 8 GPUs
- monthly_cost estimate (H100): 8 * 13.5 * 730 = $78,840
- notes: high risk; only acceptable for batch jobs where quality can be validated downstream.

Per-region summary (rounded):
- us-west1 (interactive/mixed heavy): Conservative: 9 GPUs (A100) $59k/mo; Balanced: 4 GPUs (A100) $26k/mo; Aggressive: 3 GPUs (H100) $29.6k/mo
- eu-west1 (30% of us-west demand): scale GPUs by 0.3 -> Balanced example: 1 GPU (buffer rounds up to 2) -> cost and headroom considerations
- ap-southeast1 (batch-heavy but lower peak): use aggressive batching for cost efficiency, but keep one conservative pool for sensitive customers.

Quality/regression monitoring plan:
- Eval sets: maintain a per-customer small eval harness (1000 prompts) to compute delta on: response-quality-score (0-100), token-efficiency, hallucination-rate.
- Alert thresholds: quality_delta > 3% => hold rollout, >5% => rollback to fallback model; automated canary runs on 5% of traffic.
- Logging: sample outputs for manual review; increase eval cadence for Q3/Q4 trials.

Autoscale & routing notes:
- Smart routing policy: prefer conservative variants for premium customers (tagged), route mixed traffic to Balanced variant, batch-only jobs to Aggressive variant.
- Fallback: route to FP32 model in another region if capacity saturated or regressions detected.

Open questions / risks:
- Q3 kernel maturity timeline: need benchmark suite for APAC hardware; experimental kernels exhibit nightly variance.
- Memory fragmentation when using large batch sizes with KV cache for chat; need to model context-length mix distribution (10% > 8k tokens).
- Multi-tenant contention: per-tenant isolation may require headroom higher than 20% for noisy neighbors.

Recommended next steps (action items):
- [Owner: Marcus Li] Run per-region microbenchmarks for Q4 and Q3 quant kernels on representative H100 and A100 instances (2-week sprint).
- [Owner: Elena Gomez] Expand eval harness to include hallucination-rate metric and add automated canary pipeline (ticket JIRA-INFRA-879).
- [Owner: Rahul Singh] Produce cost sensitivity analysis for spot/preemptible capacity vs reserved A100/H100 for Balanced and Aggressive scenarios.
- [Owner: Ayesha Patel] Draft rollout plan for Balanced variant as default for mixed traffic; schedule incremental canary to 5% -> 25% -> 50%.

Appendix: quick reference numbers used in calculations (for reproducibility):
- Baseline tokens/sec A100 float32 (interactive short): 1200 tps
- Q8 speedup factor: 1.6x (conservative estimate based on optimized kernels)
- Q4 speedup factor: 2.8x (observed in internal bench runs for 13B-class models)
- Q3 speedup factor: 3.6x (experimental)
- Batch speedup factors: small (1.0-1.3), moderate (1.25), large (1.8-2.0) depending on kernel and occupancy

Notes to reviewers: this is a working capacity-planning sheet. Numbers are intentionally rounded to produce simple GPU counts; the next pass should move these into an actual spreadsheet with per-request token distribution, hourly demand curves, and sensitivity scenarios for utilization and kernel variance.

Document history:
- 2024-11-15: initial draft created
- 2024-12-03: added Aggressive/H100 scenario after infra benching notes
- 2025-02-10: updated costs and added Q3 experimental scenario
